option_relations.rationale: Methimazole-induced vasculitis is a specific type of vasculitis that can manifest cutaneously, making it a subtype of cutaneous vasculitis.
Microscopic polyangiitis is a systemic vasculitis that can have cutaneous manifestations, thus it can be considered a subtype of cutaneous vasculitis when presenting in the skin.
Drug-induced ANCA-associated vasculitis is a specific form of vasculitis that can affect the skin, making it a subtype of cutaneous vasculitis.
Lupus vasculitis is a vasculitis associated with systemic lupus erythematosus that frequently involves the skin, making it a subtype of cutaneous vasculitis.
